name: Third-party clients on someone else's platform
title: Third-party apps on a platform API: still a no-go
question: Is building a third-party client on someone else's platform API viable?
answer: Apollo, a popular Reddit client, shut down on 30 June 2023 after Reddit's new API pricing would have cost it about $20M a year; Tweetbot and Twitterrific died the same way when Twitter cut off third-party clients in January 2023. Nothing about the apps changed. When the platform owns the enabler, it can take the market the moment you prove it.
verdict_reason: The platform owner controls the enabler and has used that control; nothing has changed it.

constraint.name: Platform owner controls API access
constraint.detail: The app's existence depends on terms the platform can change in a memo.

graveyard.how: Shut down 30 June 2023 after Reddit API pricing changes
